examples.en: The heady scent of lilac filled the garden.
The evening was warm and intoxicating.

note: often of a scent, music or feelings; literary and poetic

examples.sr: Осећам се [ра̀стргнут] између посла и породице.
examples.en: I feel torn between work and family.
The book had been torn to pieces.
Turn on the AC, it's hot.
The air conditioner in the room is broken.

note: colloquial, from English «air condition»; «клима» is more neutral

examples.en: Let's have a coffee before work.
My neighbor invited me over for a coffee.

note: diminutive of «кафа», warm and homey

examples.sr: Деца су на Нову годину бацала [пу̏цкалице].
examples.en: The kids threw firecrackers on New Year's.
We bought a party popper with glitter.

related.en: to shoot; to pop, to bang

examples.sr: Девојчице су се [ки̏котале] на задњем реду.
examples.en: The girls were giggling in the back row.
Stop giggling, this is serious.

note: colloquial; often «кикотати се» - to snicker at someone

examples.sr: Цео разред се [цѐрека] због његове шале.
examples.en: The whole class is howling at his joke.
What are you cackling about like a madman?

note: colloquial, sometimes a bit rude

examples.sr: Боље је да [прећу̀тим] него да се свађамо.
examples.en: It's better if I keep quiet than if we argue.
He couldn't let the insult pass in silence.

examples.sr: Само сам се мало [у̀чиркао], могу да возим.
examples.en: I only had a little to drink, I can drive.

examples.sr: После другог пића већ смо се [у̀чиркали].
examples.en: After the second round we were already tipsy.

note: colloquial, slang; mild drunkenness

examples.sr: Синоћ се [у̀рољао] и једва стигао кући.
examples.en: Last night he got hammered and barely made it home.
Don't drink any more, you'll get hammered.

note: colloquial, slang; heavy drunkenness

examples.en: Everybody got plastered at the birthday party.

examples.sr: Није хтео да се [летво̀са] пред шефом.
examples.en: He didn't want to get plastered in front of the boss.

note: colloquial, slang; rare

meanings: to get drunk (literally «to pour oneself full»)
forms: налијем се, налију се; impf. наливати се

examples.en: Everybody got drunk at the party.
He got drunk and fell asleep on the couch.

note: colloquial

examples.sr: На столу је стајао [ба̀рдак] са ракијом.
examples.en: A clay jug of rakija stood on the table.
Grandpa poured the wine from a jug.
I'm going to the pub with my buddy.

examples.sr: Мој [па̏јтос] ми је помогао да се преселим.
examples.en: My pal helped me move.

note: colloquial, slang; affectionate, for a close friend

examples.en: Look at that cute little face!

examples.sr: Пас ми је ставио [њу̏шкицу] у крило.
examples.en: The dog laid his snout in my lap.

note: diminutive of «њушка»; for animals, and affectionately for people

examples.en: Hang your jacket on the hanger.
We bought ten new hangers.

note: colloquial; a standing coat rack is «чивѝлук»

examples.sr: Скинула сам [на̏влаку] са јоргана и ставила је у машину.
examples.en: I took the cover off the duvet and put it in the washing machine.

examples.sr: Ова [на̏влака] за телефон је од коже.
examples.en: This phone case is made of leather.
Please take the cutlery to the counter.
All the cutlery is in the drawer.

note: a collective word for the whole set; from German Essgeschirr

examples.en: She wore a black beaded bracelet on her wrist.

examples.sr: Деда је у џепу чувао стару [бро̀јаницу].
examples.en: Grandpa kept an old rosary in his pocket.

note: from «бројати» - to count: the beads are counted off

examples.sr: У граду је [чѐсмуша] сасвим добра за пиће.
examples.en: The tap water in the city is perfectly fine to drink.
I don't buy bottled water, I drink tap water.

note: colloquial

examples.en: As soon as he lay down, he started snoring.
The child fell asleep and began to snore.

note: the prefix за- marks the start of the action

examples.en: We take our shoes off at the entrance.

examples.sr: Увек се [изу̀ва] пре него што уђе у кућу.
examples.en: He always takes his shoes off before he comes into the house.

note: «изувати се» - to take one's own shoes off; «изуо сам се» - I took my shoes off

forms: спремам се, спремају се; pf. спремити се

examples.en: I'm getting ready for a trip.
The children are getting ready for school.

note: with «се» - to get oneself ready; without it - to prepare something («спремати вечеру»)

examples.en: We sat on a little bench in the park.

examples.sr: Дете се попело на [клу̏пицу] да дохвати полицу.
examples.en: The child climbed onto a stool to reach the shelf.

note: diminutive of «клупа»

examples.en: As a starter I had crispy shrimp.

examples.sr: Овај ресторан је познат по [га̏мборима] на жару.
examples.en: This restaurant is known for its grilled prawns.

note: on menus usually plural: «хрскави гамбори»

examples.en: I ordered grilled cheese and a salad.
I like grilled vegetables with meat.

note: on menus: «гриловани сир», «гриловано поврће»

examples.en: I'll quickly chop the onion in the chopper.
I lent my neighbor the nut chopper.

note: colloquial; from «сецкати»: an electric bowl with a blade

examples.en: After the rain the storm drain was clogged.
Leaves covered the drain.
The actor was waiting in the wings.
The workers change the scenery between acts.

note: mostly plural: «иза кулиса» - backstage, behind the scenes

examples.sr: Гледалац је узео [ду̀рбӣн] да боље види.
examples.en: The spectator took binoculars to see better.
We watched the ship through binoculars.
The prompter whispered the line to the actor.
Without the prompter the show would have stopped.
Our seats are in the orchestra.
You can hear everything well from the orchestra.
Ćevapi are served in a warm flatbread.
Buy one flatbread for dinner.

note: a flat, fluffy bread, filled with «ћевапе» or «пљескавица»

meanings: puff pastry with a lattice top

examples.sr: У пекари сам узела [мре̏жицу] са сиром.
examples.en: At the bakery I got a lattice pastry with cheese.
This lattice pastry is still warm.

note: named after «мрежа» (net): the dough on top is cut in a lattice

examples.en: The new minister spoke about schools.
My sister became the health minister.

note: feminine job titles in -ка are normal in Serbian

examples.sr: На столу је стара [мушѐма] са цветовима.
examples.en: An old flowery oilcloth lies on the table.
Oilcloth is sold by the meter.

note: in Serbia it is often sold by the meter: «на метар»

examples.en: Take the whisk and beat the eggs.
I bought a frother for coffee.

related.en: to stir up; to whip, to beat

examples.sr: Куповином на распродаји смо [уштѐдели] много новца.
examples.en: By shopping at the sale we saved a lot of money.

examples.sr: Хоћу да [уштѐдим] за пут на море.
examples.en: I want to save up for a trip to the seaside.
I work out with five-kilogram dumbbells.

examples.sr: Купила сам пар [бу̏чица] за вежбање код куће.
examples.en: I bought a pair of dumbbells for exercising at home.

note: usually plural: «бучице»

examples.en: There's Zumba at the gym tonight.
My friend loves Zumba.
My brother snowboards on Kopaonik.

examples.sr: Прошле зиме сам први пут стао на [сно̏уборд].
examples.en: Last winter I stood on a snowboard for the first time.
The humidity is high today.

examples.sr: Због [вла̑жности] ми је тешко да дишем.
examples.en: The humidity makes it hard for me to breathe.
Add a hashtag under the photo.
This hashtag is popular now.
I had to unlock the phone.
She unblocked me after the quarrel.

meanings: to vibe (to chill and enjoy the atmosphere)

examples.sr: Лежим у кревету и [ва̑јба̄м] уз музику.
examples.en: I'm lying in bed, vibing to the music.
We vibed on the terrace all evening.

note: slang, from English «vibe»; colloquial

examples.en: I want to book a leg hair removal.
After the epilation the skin is a bit red.

note: «депилација» removes hair at the surface, «епилација» pulls it out by the root

examples.en: In winter the skin needs more moisture.
Drink water to keep your body well hydrated.
My skin is prone to acne.
This cream helps with acne.
My daughter does track and field.

examples.sr: Светско првенство у [атлѐтици] је у августу.
examples.en: The world athletics championship is in August.

examples.sr: Моја комшиница има [фѐретку] као кућног љубимца.
examples.en: My neighbor has a ferret as a pet.
A ferret is very curious.

examples.sr: Јагње се пече на [ве̏ртелу] неколико сати.
examples.en: The lamb roasts on a spit for several hours.
We celebrate May Day around the spit.

meanings: to loosen the soil with a hoe

examples.en: Grandma is hoeing the tomatoes in the garden.
In spring the beds need to be hoed.
Careful, the manhole is open!
The car fell into a manhole.

note: usually a manhole in the street

examples.sr: Он је прави [буба̀тор], све учи напамет.
examples.en: He's a real grind, he learns everything by heart.
The class called Ana a swot.

related.en: to cram, to learn by rote

note: colloquial; «штребер» is a close word, both a bit derogatory

examples.sr: Мајка је везала [си̏перак] беби око врата.
examples.en: Mother tied a bib around the baby's neck.

examples.sr: Дете је попило сок и умрљало [си̏перак].
examples.en: The child drank some juice and stained the bib.

examples.sr: Деци сваког јутра дајем [ко̑рнфлекс] са млеком.
examples.en: I give the kids cornflakes with milk every morning.
There are no more cornflakes in the box.

examples.sr: Деца су се спуштала низ брдо на [кли̏ску].
examples.en: The kids slid down the hill on a sled disc.
We bought a new sled disc for the winter.

note: colloquial variant: «пичигуз»

examples.en: Grab the sled and let's go sledding.

examples.sr: Мали се вози на [пи̏чигузу] низ брег.
examples.en: The little one slides down the hill on a sled.

note: slang; from «пичити» (to dash) + «гуза» (butt)

examples.sr: Обуци [бри̏ле] јер је сунце јако на снегу.
examples.en: Put on your goggles, the sun is strong on the snow.
He lost his goggles on the slope.

note: ski goggles: «ски наочаре» or «бриле»

examples.en: Shoo, cat, get off the table!

examples.sr: Рекла сам јој [пи̏с], али је остала на каучу.
examples.en: I told her to shoo, but she stayed on the couch.

note: «шиц» is the same, more common in Vojvodina

examples.en: Shoo, get out of the garden!

examples.sr: Баба је викнула [ши̏ц] и мачка је побегла.
examples.en: Grandma shouted shoo and the cat ran away.

note: Vojvodina; the all-Serbian word is «пис»

examples.en: Grandpa always takes the heel of the bread.

examples.sr: Није ми остала ни [кра̑јка] за доручак.
examples.en: I don't even have a crust left for breakfast.

note: in Vojvodina also «пупушка»

examples.en: Give me the heel with some butter.
The child likes the heel of the bread.

note: regional word (Vojvodina)

examples.en: Take the duster and wipe the shelves.
Mother bought a colorful feather duster.

note: from «прашина»; jokingly called «пипидастер»

examples.en: I spread cream cheese on the bread.

examples.sr: У фрижидеру има још једна кутија [кре̏мсија].
examples.en: There is one more tub of cream cheese in the fridge.

note: a brand name that became the everyday word

examples.sr: На концерту је почела [шу̏тка] испред бине.
examples.en: A mosh pit started in front of the stage at the concert.
I love the mosh pit at rock concerts.

note: from «шутирати» (to kick); «шутка» is not a joke here, that is «шала»

examples.sr: На ливади се чује [пр̀давац], али га је тешко видети.
examples.en: You can hear a corncrake in the meadow, but it's hard to see.

examples.sr: [Пр̀давац] је добио име по својим необичним звуцима.
examples.en: The corncrake got its name from its unusual sounds.

note: the name is imitative; scientific name Crex crex

examples.en: The pig stuck its snout through the fence.

examples.sr: Прасе је блатњавим [ри̏лом] рило по земљи.
examples.en: The piglet dug in the ground with its muddy snout.

note: of a person it is rude: «рило» = mug, face

examples.en: I've been hungover all day after last night's party.

examples.sr: Не пијем много јер не волим да [ма̏мура̄м].
examples.en: I don't drink much because I don't like being hungover.

note: from «мамурлук» (hangover)

examples.sr: Возач је имао преко два [про̏мила] алкохола.
examples.en: The driver had more than two per mille of alcohol in his blood.
Up to 0.2 per mille in the blood is allowed.

note: the unit ‰ (per thousand), used for blood alcohol

examples.en: My grandpa lives in the countryside.
Grandma and Grandpa are coming for the weekend.

note: the pair of «бака»

examples.en: He left his homeland as a child.
They miss their homeland a lot.

note: the homeland as a country, not a family home

examples.en: This is a formal letter to the director.
He was very formal at the meeting.

note: adverb: формално; opposite: неформално

examples.en: We're having an informal talk with the boss.
Everything here is informal and relaxed.
Can you turn the music up?
Please turn the AC up, it's cold.

note: used for volume, a device's power, intensifying

examples.en: My grandmother speaks Ukrainian.
The book has been translated into Ukrainian.
He reads poems in Belarusian.
I have a colleague who speaks Belarusian.
Her mother speaks Armenian.
This restaurant serves Armenian cuisine.
The Georgian alphabet is very beautiful.
I've been learning Georgian for a year.

examples.sr: На Косову се говори [а̀лбански] и српски.
examples.en: Albanian and Serbian are spoken in Kosovo.
He learned Albanian at school.
Give me a pen, I'll sign.
My pen doesn't write anymore.

note: short for «хемијска оловка»

examples.en: I always confide my secrets to him.
My boss entrusts me with the most important jobs.

note: not «to believe» (веровати) but «to entrust, to confide»

examples.en: Children notice every detail.
I don't notice any difference between them.
A yellow nasturtium is blooming on the terrace.

examples.sr: Латице [дра̏гољуба] могу да се једу у салати.
examples.en: Nasturtium petals can be eaten in a salad.

note: also a man's name, Драгољуб

examples.en: The new app brings all your accounts together.
This project combines the work of three teams.

note: bookish; mostly in formal style

examples.en: I brought a colorful matryoshka from Russia.

examples.sr: У [ба̀бушки] има још пет мањих лутака.
examples.en: There are five smaller dolls inside the matryoshka.

examples.sr: Његова [бѐседа] на конференцији била је веома дирљива.
examples.en: His speech at the conference was very moving.

examples.sr: Свештеник је одржао кратку [бѐседу] после службе.
examples.en: The priest gave a short sermon after the service.

note: bookish, solemn; in daily life it's «разговор»

examples.sr: Он је прави [сре̏ћковић], свуда има среће.
examples.en: He's a real lucky devil, he has luck everywhere.

examples.sr: Ти си [сре̏ћковић], нашао си новчаницу на улици!
examples.en: You lucky guy, you found a banknote on the street!

note: jocular; sounds like a surname (suffix -овић)

examples.sr: Не прилази му, он је прави [первѐрзња̄к].
examples.en: Don't go near him, he's a real pervert.
Everyone considered him a pervert.

note: rude, colloquial

examples.sr: Он је велики [манипула̀тор], не верујте му.
examples.en: He's a great manipulator, don't trust him.

examples.sr: Њена сестра је [манипула̀тор] и увек добије шта хоће.
examples.en: Her sister is a manipulator and always gets what she wants.
She left her abuser.
The police arrested the abuser.

examples.sr: Мој ујак је цео живот остао [нѐжења].
examples.en: My uncle stayed a bachelor all his life.

examples.sr: Он је стари [нѐжења] и живи сам.
examples.en: He's an old bachelor and lives alone.

note: masculine, but declines like nouns in -а

meanings: maybe some other time (a polite way out of an invitation)

examples.sr: Хвала на позиву, [мо̀жда не̏кӣ дру̏гӣ пу̑т].
examples.en: Thanks for the invitation, maybe some other time.

examples.sr: Идемо на роштиљ? — [Мо̀жда не̏кӣ дру̏гӣ пу̑т].
examples.en: Shall we go for a barbecue? - Maybe some other time.

note: Formally a promise of another time, in practice often a soft «probably not».

meanings: I'm not sure. We'll see. (a soft way to dodge an answer)
forms: literally: I am not sure, we will see

examples.en: Are you coming tomorrow? - Not sure. We'll see.

examples.sr: Хоћеш ли са нама на море? — [Ни́сам си̏гӯран]. Јавићу ти.
examples.en: Do you want to come to the seaside with us? - Not sure. I'll let you know.

note: A very soft form: usually means «probably not», without a direct refusal.

meanings: I probably won't be able to (a polite refusal)
forms: literally: hard that I will be able

examples.sr: Вечерас је журка, али [те̑шко да ћу мо̏ћи].
examples.en: There's a party tonight, but I probably won't be able to make it.
I probably won't get there by eight.

note: Practically a flat refusal, just worded softly.

meanings: must have, surely (a guess about the past)

examples.en: He must have forgotten the keys.
It must have been hard.

note: «мора да» + verb is a confident guess: «мора да је дошао» - he must have come. From a line in the film «Ми нисмо анђели».

key: phr:у мени су и анђео и ђаво
meanings: good and evil live together in me; I'm a contradictory person
forms: literally: in me are both an angel and a devil

examples.sr: Не знам шта хоћу, у мени су [и а̑нђео и ђа̏во̄].
examples.en: I don't know what I want, I have both an angel and a devil in me.

note: A famous line from the cult comedy «Ми нисмо анђели» (1992); the hero speaks about his inner conflict.

meanings: the wrong door: to go to the wrong person

examples.sr: Ако тражиш да ти ја дам пара, куцаш на [по̀грешна вра́та].
examples.en: If you're asking me for money, you're knocking on the wrong door.

examples.sr: Мислио је да ће му она помоћи, али је покуцао на [по̀грешна вра́та].
examples.en: He thought she would help him, but he knocked on the wrong door.

note: «врата» is always plural, even for one door; the usual phrase is «покуцати на погрешна врата».

meanings: doubtful, but okay; fine, let it be

examples.sr: Каже да је цео дан учио? [Су̏мњиво, а̏ли у ре̑ду].
examples.en: He says he studied all day? Doubtful, but okay.

examples.sr: Нова фризура, нови стил... [Су̏мњиво, а̏ли у ре̑ду].
examples.en: A new haircut, a new style... Doubtful, but okay.

note: A joking colloquial reply: you doubt it but won't argue.

examples.en: Last night we had ćevapi, the food was awesome!
Grandma always has amazing food.

note: In slang «брутално» means «very cool, powerful»; «клопа» is colloquial for «food, grub».

meanings: electric circuit; in a joke - a circle of forks, since «коло» is also a folk dance

examples.en: The circuit is broken.

note: A pun from a slide: forks dancing the «коло». Seriously, «струјно коло» is a physics term.

meanings: I'm okay today, I feel fine

examples.sr: [Да̀нас сам о̀кеј], само сам мало уморан.
examples.en: I'm okay today, just a little tired.
Don't worry, I'm fine today.

note: «океј» is common in casual speech; the phrase says «no drama today».

examples.en: Sorry, I'm in a hurry, I'll message you later.
Sorry, I'm rushing to catch a bus.

note: a polite way to cut a talk short; to strangers and elders: «извините, журим».

meanings: let's go for a drink (a coffee, a glass)
forms: literally: let's go for a drink

examples.en: Let's go for a drink after work!

examples.sr: Данас је леп дан, [а̀јмо на пи́ће].
examples.en: It's a nice day today, let's go for a drink.

note: «пиће» is not necessarily alcohol: it invites you to sit in a café or bar.

examples.en: I'm tired today, everybody back off!
Everybody out of my room!

note: a rude, joking command, like «shoo»; fine among friends, not with the boss.

examples.sr: [До̀бро ју̏тро, до̏брӣ љу̏ди]! Како сте спавали?
examples.en: Good morning, everyone! How did you sleep?

examples.sr: [До̀бро ју̏тро, до̏брӣ љу̏ди], нови дан је пред нама.
examples.en: Good morning, everyone, a new day is ahead of us.

note: a typical start of morning cards in messengers: «добри људи» addresses everybody at once.

meanings: welcome to a new day (a morning wish)
forms: literally: welcome to a new day

examples.en: Welcome to a new day, friends!
Get up, welcome to a new day!

note: a stock caption of morning cards; coffee usually follows.

meanings: the coffee is ready, come and have a cup
forms: literally: the little coffee is ready

examples.en: Good morning, the coffee is ready!
Sit down, the coffee is ready.

forms: literally: a little coffee for you, here you go

examples.sr: [Ка̏фица за те̏бе, изво̀ли], још је топла.
examples.en: Here's your coffee, it's still hot.
Have some coffee, my dear.

note: «изволи» (informal), «изволите» (formal): said when serving or handing something over.

examples.en: Good morning, enjoy your coffee!
Sit down, I made you a nice coffee.

note: modeled on «пријатно» (bon appétit).

meanings: we have our ups and downs (in life, in business)
forms: literally: we have both rises and falls

examples.sr: У сваком браку [и̏ма и у̏спона и па̏дова].
examples.en: Every marriage has its ups and downs.

examples.sr: Фирма је [и̏мала и у̏споне и па̏дове].
examples.en: The company had its ups and downs.

note: «пад» is a fall, pl. «падови»; here it is the opposite of «успон».

meanings: we're drowning in problems, there are too many

examples.en: This month we're drowning in problems.
He's been floundering in problems for a long time.

note: the preposition «у» takes the locative: «у проблемима».

meanings: to give up, to admit defeat
forms: literally: to raise a white flag

examples.sr: Брже него што смо мислили, [ди̏гли смо бе̑лу за̏ставу].
examples.en: Faster than we thought, we gave up.

examples.sr: Не желим да [ди̏гнем бе̑лу за̏ставу] после првог пораза.
examples.en: I don't want to give up after the first defeat.

note: «дићи» or «дигнути»: both forms are in use.

key: phr:далеко, далеко срце ми је остало
meanings: my heart stayed far away (homesickness, longing for the past)
forms: literally: far, far my heart stayed

examples.sr: Живим у иностранству, али [ср̏це ми је о̀стало] у Београду.
examples.en: I live abroad, but my heart stayed in Belgrade.
My heart stayed by the sea.

note: a line in the spirit of Yugo-nostalgia: «срце ми је остало» is how you speak of a place you miss.

meanings: to think you are the center of the world, that everything revolves around you
forms: literally: the world spins around someone

examples.sr: Ти мислиш да се [све̑т вр̏ти о̏ко те̏бе]?
examples.en: Do you think the world revolves around you?

examples.sr: Није тачно да се [све̑т вр̏ти о̏ко] њега.
examples.en: It's not true that the world revolves around him.

note: usually a reproach to a selfish person.

meanings: my brain freezes, I can't think (e.g. in the heat)

examples.sr: Лети од врућине [мо̏зак ми се блокѝра].
examples.en: In summer my brain freezes from the heat.

examples.sr: Кад сам уморан, [мо̏зак ми се блокѝра].
examples.en: When I'm tired, my brain freezes.

note: Colloquial; also «мозак ми не ради» - my brain isn't working.

meanings: «and I you», the reply to «волим те»; in a joking series of pictures - the answer to any question, meaning «you're dear to me»

examples.en: - I love you. - And I you.
- How are you? - And I you (meaning «I'm thinking of you too»).

note: A series of pictures: to every question the hero answers «и ја тебе» - a Serbian joke about love without big words.

meanings: little things matter, every small act of care counts

examples.sr: Јавио ми се да пита како сам - [ма̑ле ства̏ри се бро̑је].
examples.en: He messaged to ask how I was - the little things count.

examples.sr: Није скупо, али [ма̑ле ства̏ри се бро̑је].
examples.en: It's not expensive, but the little things count.

note: From a picture caption: showing love and care is easy, and in hard times small things matter most.

meanings: we'll figure something out, we'll find a way

examples.en: Don't worry, we'll figure something out.

examples.sr: Нема аута, али [смѝслићемо ми] како да стигнемо.
examples.en: There's no car, but we'll figure out how to get there.

note: «ми» adds emphasis: it's us, together, who will sort it out.

meanings: what we don't know makes us afraid
forms: literally: ignorance gives birth to fear

examples.en: Ignorance breeds fear, so we learn.
It's often true that ignorance breeds fear.

note: A stencil on a wall in Belgrade; short-thought graffiti like this is common in the city.

key: phr:прећутао бих цео свет због тебе
meanings: for you I would stay silent in front of the whole world
forms: literally: I would keep silent the whole world because of you

examples.en: I would put up with everything in silence for you.
For you I would let an insult pass in silence.

note: Graffiti on a ruined wall; an example of the conditional: «бих» + past participle in -о/-ла.

meanings: brain rot: mindless content that melts your brain

examples.sr: Цео дан гледам видео-клипове, права је то [тру̀љеж мо̏зга].
examples.en: I watch videos all day, it's real brain rot.

note: youth slang, a calque of English «brain rot»

examples.en: You answered correctly, high five!
Deal, high five.

note: said for a friendly slap of palms; also «дај пет».

examples.sr: Сутра ћемо имати [де̏војачко ве̏че̄] за Миру.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll have a bachelorette party for Mira.
Where will you celebrate the bachelorette party?

note: the bride's party with her friends before the wedding.

examples.en: His friends organized a bachelor party for him.
Nobody drank at the bachelor party.

note: the groom's party with friends before the wedding; the pair of «девојачко вече».

meanings: get it? you know what I mean? (colloquial)

examples.en: I don't want to go there, get it?
I don't get what you're trying to say.

note: From Italian via slang; the verb «капирати» - to get, to understand. Informal only, with equals.

meanings: sort of, kind of, as if

examples.en: He said it sort of as a joke.

examples.sr: Дошла је [у фа̀зону] да нас обиђе.
examples.en: She came by sort of to visit us.

note: A colloquial filler: the action looks like something or is done «in the manner of» it. Not the same as «бити у фазону» (to be in the mood).

forms: literally: let me tell you honestly

examples.sr: [Да ти ка̏жем и̏скрено], не свиђа ми се тај план.
examples.en: To be honest, I don't like that plan.

examples.sr: [Да ти ка̏жем и̏скрено], нисам очекивао толико људи.
examples.en: Frankly, I didn't expect so many people.

note: An intro to an honest opinion, between people on «ти» terms. Polite form: «Да вам кажем искрено».

meanings: I mean, like, you know (filler words)
forms: literally: well I think, you know

examples.sr: [Па ми̏слӣм, зна̑ш], није то баш лако.
examples.en: I mean, you know, it's not exactly easy.

examples.sr: Ја, [па ми̏слӣм, зна̑ш], не знам шта да кажем.
examples.en: I, like, don't know what to say.

note: A pause filler while you look for words. Not needed in writing.

examples.en: The child's nose is running, give him a tissue.
My nose has been running since this morning.

note: «цурити» - to trickle in a thin stream; also said of a leaking tap: «Цури славина».

meanings: tooth fairy (takes away a fallen baby tooth)

examples.sr: Остави зуб под јастук, доћи ће [зу̀бић ви̏ла].
examples.en: Put the tooth under your pillow, the tooth fairy will come.

note: «Зубић» is a diminutive of «зуб»; «вила» is a fairy or woodland nymph from folk tales.

meanings: to purse one's lips (duck face); to pout
forms: literally: to puff out the lips

examples.en: She purses her lips in every photo.
The child started to pout.

note: The verb «пућити»: он пући, она пући. Also said of sulking.

forms: literally: I did not hear well

examples.sr: Извините, [ни́сам до̀бро чу̏о], можете ли поновити?
examples.en: Excuse me, I didn't catch that, could you repeat it?
I didn't catch your name.

note: A polite request to repeat. You can add «Молим?» or «Како, молим?».

meanings: to lose it, to snap from anger
forms: literally: the roller shutter falls on me

examples.sr: Кад чујем ту причу, [па̑дне ми ролѐтна].
examples.en: When I hear that story, I just snap with anger.

examples.sr: Само да ми не [па̑дне ролѐтна] пред шефом.
examples.en: I just hope I don't lose it in front of the boss.

note: A colloquial image: as if a shutter comes down inside and reason switches off.

examples.en: The kids ask for cotton candy at the fair.
I bought my daughter pink cotton candy.

note: «Вуна» is wool: the candy looks like a ball of wool.

examples.en: The child caught measles.
There is a vaccine against measles.

note: «Богиње» - pox, «мале богиње» - measles, «овчије богиње» - chickenpox. The singular «богиња» is a goddess.

meanings: that's how things stand, that's the situation

examples.sr: Не волим то да кажем, али [та̀ко̄ сто̀је̄ ства̏ри].
examples.en: I don't like to say it, but that's how things stand.
The project is late, that's how things are.

note: Sums up a conversation.

forms: literally: every day is a holiday

examples.sr: Кад си међу пријатељима, [сва̏кӣ да̑н је пра̑знӣк].
examples.en: When you're among friends, every day is a holiday.

examples.sr: Мом деди је [сва̏кӣ да̑н пра̑знӣк] у башти.
examples.en: For my grandpa every day in the garden is a holiday.

note: A slogan-wish: treat ordinary days as a reason to be glad.

examples.en: We spent the summer on the Côte d'Azur.
The Côte d'Azur is expensive for us.

note: The name of a region in France, written «Азурна обала» with capitals. «Азурни» means azure, sky blue.

meanings: God help me! (when everything is falling apart or you have no strength)

examples.en: The flight is canceled again, God help me!

examples.sr: Погледај колики је ово хаос, [помо̀зи, Бо̏же]!
examples.en: Look what a mess this is, good Lord!

note: A half-joking exclamation of tiredness or bewilderment, not necessarily religious.

meanings: leave me a message, text me
forms: literally: let a message go to me

examples.en: I can't talk now, text me.
If you get there earlier, drop me a message.

note: A message is «пустити» (let go), as if sent on its way; also «оставити поруку».

meanings: you're a sweetheart, you're a gem (affectionate, thankful)

examples.en: Thanks for coming, you're a sweetheart!
You brought me coffee, you're a darling!

note: Colloquial praise to a close person; said to a woman or a man.

meanings: I'm keeping my fingers crossed for you
forms: literally: I hold figs for you

examples.sr: Сутра ти је испит, [др̀жӣм ти фи̏ге]!
examples.en: You have an exam tomorrow, fingers crossed for you!
We're keeping our fingers crossed for you at the interview.

note: Serbs hold «фиге» (a fist with the thumb between two fingers) rather than crossing their fingers.

meanings: let life go on, life goes on

examples.sr: Било је тешко, али [не̏к и̏де жѝвот]!
examples.en: It was hard, but life goes on!
Don't worry, life goes on!

note: A cheerful motto of staying calm about trouble; «нек» is colloquial for «нека».

meanings: it won't help, it's no use
forms: literally: there will be no use

examples.en: If you don't study, it's no use.
Begging won't help, the decision has been made.

note: Short colloquial form of «неће бити вајде». «Вајда» - use, benefit.

meanings: no way, not by any means

examples.sr: Да ли ћеш му позајмити новац? — [Ни слу̏ча̄јно]!
examples.en: Will you lend him money? - No way!

examples.sr: Таква грешка [ни слу̏ча̄јно] не сме да се понови.
examples.en: Such a mistake must under no circumstances happen again.

note: A sharp refusal; the gesture is crossed arms.

meanings: I'll go crazy (from noise, tiredness, anger)

examples.en: This crowd is unbearable, I'll go crazy!
If this goes on for another hour, I'll go nuts.

note: Future of «полудети». Not strong: also said of minor annoyances.

examples.en: It's already eight, you're late!
You're late for work again.

note: «Касни(ти)» - to be late or slow: «касни воз», «сат касни».

examples.en: Call me when you arrive!
If you need anything, call me.

note: In colloquial speech «назвати некога» means to phone someone; «позвати» is also used.

meanings: oh no, what have I done?!
forms: literally: oh, what did I do

examples.sr: Пребацила сам новац погрешном човеку. [Јо̑ј! Шта̏ сам у̀радила?!]
examples.en: I sent the money to the wrong person. Oh no, what have I done?!

examples.sr: Заборавила сам кључеве у стану, [јо̑ј, шта̏ сам у̀радила]!
examples.en: I forgot the keys in the apartment, oh no, what have I done!

note: Feminine form «урадила»; a man says «урадио». «Јој» is an interjection of distress.

examples.en: The bus has left, so now what?
We've finished everything. What next?

note: Longer variants: «шта сад да радимо?», «и шта сад?».

examples.sr: Фотографија је лоша, на њој сам [ру́жан ка̏о ло́пов].
examples.en: The photo is bad, I look hideous in it.

examples.sr: Он је [ру́жан ка̏о ло́пов], али има добро срце.
examples.en: He's ugly as sin, but he has a good heart.

note: A set comparison: «ружан» changes by gender (ружна као лопов), «лопов» stays. Jocular and a bit rude; not said to someone's face.

examples.sr: Значи, сви долазе у суботу? — [Та̀ко̄ је].
examples.en: So everyone is coming on Saturday? - Exactly.

examples.sr: Цена је превисока. — [Та̀ко̄ је], слажем се.
examples.en: The price is too high. - That's right, I agree.

note: A short confirmation or agreement; at speeches and meetings it is often shouted in support.

meanings: to cross off the list, to take off the list
forms: literally: to take off the list

examples.sr: Купио сам хлеб, [ски̏ни] га са списка.
examples.en: I bought the bread, take it off the list.

examples.sr: Ако не можеш да дођеш, [ски̏ни] се са списка.
examples.en: If you can't come, take yourself off the list.

note: Seen on signs and in apps («Скините са списка»); on paper also «прецртати».

examples.en: A pile-up happened on the highway.

examples.sr: У магли је дошло до [ла̏нчаног су̏дара] осам возила.
examples.en: In the fog, eight vehicles collided in a pile-up.

note: based on «ланац» - chain

examples.en: I'm sending the parcel by express mail.
Express mail arrives in two days.

note: written on parcels when fast delivery is needed

examples.en: The pedestrian path goes this way.

examples.sr: Бицикли не смеју на [ста̏зу за пѐшаке].
examples.en: Bicycles are not allowed on the pedestrian path.

note: a sign near summer terraces and in parks; «стаза» - path, trail

meanings: registration sticker: a hologram sticker on the windshield showing the car's registration is valid for a year

examples.en: The new registration sticker is valid for a year.
I stuck the registration sticker on the windshield.

note: In Serbia you get it after the technical inspection and the renewal of the car's registration («регистрација»).

meanings: it matters, it makes a difference
forms: literally: it is not all the same

examples.en: It matters to me what he will say.

examples.sr: Када се ради о здрављу, [нѝје свејѐдно] шта једеш.
examples.en: When it comes to health, it matters what you eat.

note: a slogan on a juice package: the choice matters; «свеједно» - all the same, no difference

examples.en: Here we are, we made it!
Hi, here we are at the party.

note: modeled on «ево ме» (here I am); «ево вас» - here you are

meanings: watch your head (a warning at a low ceiling or beam)

examples.en: There's a low beam here, watch your head!

examples.sr: На степеницама је плафон низак, [па̏зи ву̏гла].
examples.en: The ceiling on the stairs is low, watch your head.

note: A sign on the stairs of a café in Novi Sad. «Вугла» is slang for head, a reshaping of «глава» in the style of «шатровачки» slang (syllable play). Jocular, colloquial.

meanings: let's move on, let's go on (in a story, a trip, a program)

examples.en: We're done with this, let's move on.
Thanks for the question, let's move on.

note: Works for a literal journey (we drive on) and for moving to the next topic.

examples.en: Throw the paper in the trash can.

note: On the street this is the litter bin; at home more often «канта за смеће».

examples.en: Where is the fitting room?

note: A phrase for a clothing store; politely: «Могу ли да пробам?» (May I try it on?).

examples.en: The escalator isn't working.

note: The word «ескалатор» is understood too, but signs usually say «покретне степенице».

examples.en: I'd like a slice of rye bread with butter.

note: bakeries often call it «црни хлеб» too; plain white is «бели хлеб»

examples.sr: Дајте ми један [ро̑л ви̏ршла] и јогурт.
examples.en: Give me one sausage roll and a yogurt.

note: a typical bakery snack, grabbed on the go; «виршла» - a wiener, frankfurter

meanings: without a ton of money; when there is not enough money at all
forms: literally: without a mountain of money

examples.sr: Тешко је живети [без бр̏да па̑ра] у великом граду.
examples.en: It's hard to live in a big city without a ton of money.

examples.sr: Да имам [бр̏до па̑ра], не бих радио.
examples.en: If I had a ton of money, I wouldn't work.

note: «брдо» in colloquial speech means «a pile, a lot»: «брдо пара» - loads of money, «брдо ствари» - a mountain of things.

meanings: to withdraw money from an account or card

examples.sr: Банка ми неће [ски̏нути па̑ре] ако их немам.
examples.en: The bank can't take money from me if I don't have any.
I need to withdraw money from my card.

note: Colloquial; in formal speech more often «подићи новац».

meanings: special offer, sale (on a price tag or banner)

examples.sr: Ове недеље траје [спе̏ција̄лна по̏нуда] на све кишобране.
examples.en: This week there's a special offer on all umbrellas.

examples.sr: Видела сам [спѐцијалну по̏нуду] у радњи поред куће.
examples.en: I saw a special offer in the shop next to my house.

note: Next to it on signs you see «попуст» (discount) and «распродаја» (sale).

meanings: you rock, you're killing it, that came out great

examples.en: You rock! You played really well.
Bro, you're killing it on stage!

note: slang praise: someone does something at the top level. Said to friends, jokingly or seriously.

examples.sr: Молим вас, две [ко̏цке ше̏ћера] у чај.
examples.en: Two sugar cubes in my tea, please.

examples.sr: Обично не стављам [ко̏цку ше̏ћера] у кафу.
examples.en: I usually don't put a sugar cube in my coffee.

note: In Serbia sugar is often served in cubes with coffee and tea; counted as «коцке».

meanings: how long does the treatment take?
forms: literally: how long does the procedure last

examples.en: How long does a facial treatment take?

examples.sr: Реците ми, [колѝко тра̑је трѐтма̄н] и колико кошта.
examples.en: Tell me, how long does the treatment take and how much does it cost?

note: «траје» - from «трајати» (to last).

meanings: how often do the buses run?
forms: literally: how often do the buses go

examples.en: How often do buses run to the center?

examples.sr: Не знам [колѝко че̑сто и̑ду а̀утобуси] викендом.
examples.en: I don't know how often the buses run on weekends.

note: «ред вожње» - timetable.

meanings: when are we finally going to (start ...)?
forms: literally: when will we already finally ...

examples.sr: [Ка̏да ћемо ве̏ћ јѐдно̄м] почети да носимо летњу одећу?
examples.en: When will we finally start wearing summer clothes?

examples.sr: [Ка̏да ћемо ве̏ћ јѐдно̄м] отићи на море?
examples.en: When will we finally go to the seaside?

note: «већ једном» - finally, at last: impatience or a joking complaint; the verb is in the future tense.

key: phr:можеш ли ми показати како се ради ова вежба
meanings: can you show me how to do this exercise?
forms: literally: can you show me how this exercise is done

examples.sr: [Мо̀жеш ли ми пока́зати ка̏ко се ра̑ди о̀ва̄ вѐжба]?
examples.en: Can you show me how to do this exercise?

examples.sr: Тренеру, [мо̀жете ли ми пока́зати ка̏ко се ра̑ди] чучањ?
examples.en: Coach, can you show me how to do a squat?

note: «радити вежбу» - to do an exercise (not «правити»).

key: phr:дајте му овај лек два пута дневно
meanings: give him this medicine twice a day
forms: literally: give him this medicine two times daily

examples.sr: [Да̑јте му о̀ва̄ј ле̑к два̑ пу̑та дне̑вно] после јела.
examples.en: Give him this medicine twice a day after meals.

examples.sr: Ветеринар каже: [да̑јте му о̀ва̄ј ле̑к два̑ пу̑та дне̑вно].
examples.en: The vet says: give him this medicine twice a day.

note: «пута» after numbers: «два пута, три пута»; «дневно» - daily.

meanings: summer is a state of mind
forms: literally: summer is a state of mind

examples.sr: За мене [ле̏то је ста́ње у̑ма], чак и у новембру.
examples.en: For me summer is a state of mind, even in November.
Don't rush, summer is a state of mind.

note: A caption on a greeting card. «Стање ума» - a state of mind or mood.

forms: literally: I gather moments, and not things

examples.sr: Путујем лако: [са̀купљам трену́тке, а не ства̏ри].
examples.en: I travel light: I collect moments, not things.

examples.sr: Мој мото је [са̀купљам трену́тке, а не ства̏ри].
examples.en: My motto is: I collect moments, not things.

note: A nice caption for a vacation photo; «ствари» - things.

meanings: the coffee won't drink itself (time to get going, come to the table)
forms: literally: the coffee will not drink itself

examples.en: Sit down, the coffee won't drink itself.

examples.sr: [Ше́тња се нѐће са̀ма о̀бавити], хајде да идемо.
examples.en: The walk won't take itself, let's go.

note: A joking card phrase: «X се неће сам(а) Y» - X won't get done by itself, time to start. Seen on «Добро јутро» cards.

examples.en: Call any number from the list.
Take any book.

note: only «који» declines: било ког, било коме; stress on «било» and «који». For people there is «било ко» (anyone).

meanings: there is no death, there is only a passage (a soul or a people moves on)
forms: literally: death does not exist, there is migration

examples.sr: Писац је рекао: [смр̏ти не̑ма, и̑ма сѐоба].
examples.en: The writer said: there is no death, only migration.
I'm reading «Migrations», a novel about the great migration of the Serbs.

note: A quote from the writer Miloš Crnjanski (the novel «Сеобе»). «Сеоба» - migration, exodus; the word often speaks of a people's fate.

key: phr:са природом се споји, свој живот кроји
meanings: unite with nature and tailor your own life (slogan of an eco brochure)
forms: literally: unite with nature, cut your life

examples.en: I want to shape my own life.

examples.sr: Викендом се [спа̑јам са при̏родом] на планини.
examples.en: On weekends I merge with nature in the mountains.

note: A rhymed call (споји - кроји). «Кројити живот» - literally to tailor: to arrange your fate as you wish.

meanings: are you out of your mind? (about odd, inappropriate behavior)

examples.sr: [Је̑ л' си је̏о бу̀нике]? Не можеш тако да вичеш!
examples.en: Are you out of your mind? You can't shout like that!
What are you doing, have you lost your mind?

note: «Бунике» - henbane, a poisonous plant: whoever eats it acts mad. «Је л'» is a colloquial short form of «јеси ли».

meanings: Excuse me, I'm a foreigner (when you did not understand)
forms: literally: excuse me, I am a foreigner

examples.sr: Извините, ја сам [стра́нац], можете ли да говорите спорије?
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm a foreigner, could you speak more slowly?

note: A polite way to ask for help or for slower speech.

meanings: I wouldn't; no thanks (a soft refusal)

examples.en: I wouldn't do anything like that.

examples.sr: Да сам на твом месту, [не бих] ишао.
examples.en: If I were you, I wouldn't go.

note: The conditional: бих + participle. Sounds softer than «нећу».

meanings: forget it; don't even think about it (a sharp refusal)

examples.en: A new car? Forget it, we have no money.

note: A colloquial refusal; in the same row: «нема шансе» and «не бих».

meanings: no open fires, making fires is prohibited

examples.en: Making fires is prohibited in the forest.

note: A typical sign in forests and parks. The verb «ложити» here means to light, to kindle.

key: phr:могу ли да добијем једну кафу, молим вас
meanings: a polite request for a coffee in a café
forms: literally: can I get one coffee, please

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем јѐдну ка̏фу], молим вас?
examples.en: Can I have a coffee, please?

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем ка̏фу] са млеком?
examples.en: Can I have a coffee with milk?

note: Shorter and more usual: «Једну кафу, молим.» «Могу ли да замолим…» is even more polite.

key: phr:можете ли ми додати мало шећера
meanings: a request to add a little sugar
forms: literally: can you add me a little sugar

examples.sr: [Мо̀жете ли ми до̀дати ма̏ло ше̏ћера], молим вас?
examples.en: Could you add a little sugar, please?

examples.sr: [Мо̀жете ли ми до̀не̄ти] још једну кафу?
examples.en: Could you bring me another coffee?

note: «Можете ли ми» + infinitive is a universal polite request; «мало» is followed by the genitive.

forms: literally: do you have decaffeinated coffee

examples.en: Do you have decaf coffee?

examples.sr: [Да ли и̑мате] соје млеко за капућино?
examples.en: Do you have soy milk for a cappuccino?

note: «Да ли имате…?» is the standard question about availability; decaf isn't found everywhere in Serbia.

examples.en: The airbag deployed in the collision.
This car has six airbags.

note: The same «јастук» as an ordinary pillow for sleeping.

examples.sr: [Мѐра̄ч го̀рива] показује да је резервоар скоро празан.
examples.en: The fuel gauge shows the tank is almost empty.
Look at the fuel gauge before the trip.

note: The pattern «мерач» + genitive: «мерач температуре» - temperature gauge.

forms: literally: little lever of the gearbox

examples.sr: Ухватио је [ру̀чицу мења́ча] и пребацио у другу.
examples.en: He grabbed the gear lever and shifted into second.
The gear lever moves stiffly.
Buy toothpaste and soap.

examples.sr: Ова [па̏ста за зу̑бе] има укус нане.
examples.en: This toothpaste tastes of mint.

note: The pattern «за» + accusative plural: «за зубе» (for teeth).

examples.en: I have a business meeting at nine.
The business meeting has been moved to tomorrow.
I need a formal suit for the wedding.
Everyone came in formal wear.
I forgot my toothbrush.

examples.sr: Ова [че̏ткица за зу̑бе] је превише тврда.
examples.en: This toothbrush is too hard.

note: Plain «четка» is a brush for clothes or hair.

examples.en: The referee showed the forward a yellow card.

examples.sr: Добио је други [жу̑тӣ ка̀рто̄н] и црвени.
examples.en: He got a second yellow card and then a red one.

note: «Картон» is cardboard; a bank card is «картица».

examples.en: The referee awarded a free kick.
He scored a goal from a free kick.
